localChanges: Automated Settlers, and computer players' workers, now plant Forest on dry Grassland or Plains that a city with food to spare and few shields is working, once they've run out of better jobs (#428).
They also irrigate Hills beside water to carry it on to a dry square worth irrigating, and mine the Hills once that square has water (closes #428).

log: Planting Forest (`plantingJobs`): on a worked Grassland or Plains square with no feature, irrigation or mine that no water could ever reach (`couldHaveWater`), for a city with at least 3 food and at most 2 shields to spare. It's worth Forest's yields less the square's, and less a Road's trade. A planted Forest never has water beside it, so it's never cleared again.

Hills with no mine can now carry water (`couldCarryWater`): irrigating them is worth half of the dry neighbour's irrigation as well, `onlyWaterFor` keeps them unmined until the neighbour is irrigated, and a mine already there is never given up for it.

A city's food and shield surplus is kept once a turn (`surplusFor`), which `weightsFor` now uses too. In the arena (80 games x 300 turns, seeds 1-40 and 41-80, against dfa8b95) no metric is worse at |t| >= 2; computer players rarely run out of better jobs, so these mostly serve a player's Automated Settlers (civ-clone/web-renderer#428).

Planting now needs no source of water within three squares (`waterNear`, replacing `couldHaveWater` there): water two squares off, or a Jungle or Swamp beside the square that could be cleared and irrigated, could otherwise reach the Forest later and have it cleared again.

Forest already being planted for the same city by another worker counts against its surplus: each one is a point of food fewer and a shield more. The planting value compares the square's yields now with the Forest's, so a Railroad's share is counted as well as a Road's trade, and a city's own square is never planted.

Tests cover the Road and Railroad values, the shield threshold, the feature, irrigation and mine exclusions, both ways water could arrive, plantings under way, and mined Hills outside the city's squares not being sent a worker (civ-clone/web-renderer#428).
